'''Bernard Roizman''' (April 17, 1929 – April 13, 2026) was an American scientist. He was the Joseph Regenstein Distinguished Service Professor of [[Virology]] in the Department of [[Microbiology]] and Department of [[Molecular Genetics]] and [[Cell Biology]] at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref name="uc">{{cite web |title=Bernard Roizman |url=https://microbiology.uchicago.edu/page/bernard-roizman |website=The University of Chicago |access-date=3 January 2019}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Roizman was born in [[Chișinău]], [[Kingdom of Romania]], in 1929. As he later recalled, his early life was "shaped by World War II"<ref name="roizman">{{cite journal |last1=Roizman |first1=Bernard |title=The Maturation of a Scientist: An Autobiography |journal=Annual Review of Virology |date=9 November 2015 |volume=2 |issue=1 |pages=1–23 |doi=10.1146/annurev-virology-100114-054829|pmid=26958904}}</ref>  and the hardships his family endured as [[war refugees]] after being displaced in 1941 by the [[German invasion of the Soviet Union]]. The family eventually made their way to the United States in 1948, where they settled in [[Philadelphia]].<ref name=roizman /> Roizman received a scholarship to attend a Pennsylvanian college and enrolled at [[Temple University]], from which he received his bachelor's and master's degrees. He subsequently attended the [[Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health|Johns Hopkins School of Public Health]], where he received his Sc.D. in 1956.<ref name=uc /><ref name=roizman />

==Academic career and research==
Roizman joined the faculty at Johns Hopkins after graduation, and later spent a year as a visiting scientist at the [[Institut Pasteur]] in Paris.<ref name=roizman /> When he returned to the United States he joined the faculty at the [[University of Chicago]] in 1965.<ref name=uc /><ref name=roizman /> He served as department chair from 1985 to 1988.<ref name="jhu">{{cite web |title=Bernard Roizman, ScD |url=https://www.jhsph.edu/about/history/heroes-of-public-health/bernard-roizman.html |website=Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health |access-date=3 January 2019}}</ref> He was one of several prominent virologists involved in the founding of the [[American Society for Virology]] and organized a key meeting in Chicago that led to the society's establishment.<ref name=joklik>{{cite journal |vauthors=Joklik WK, Grossberg SE |title=How the American Society for Virology was founded |journal=Virology |volume=344 |issue=1 |pages=250–7 |year=2006 |pmid=16364755 |doi=10.1016/j.virol.2005.09.022 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Roizman's research interests focused on the [[herpes simplex virus]], particularly on [[gene regulation|regulation]] of viral genes and on the use of [[site-specific mutagenesis]] to study viral gene function.<ref name=roizman /><ref name=jhu /> In 1999 he was involved in an [[inventorship]] dispute with a member of his research group, whose lawsuit was ultimately successful.<ref name="duke">{{cite journal |last1=Grimshaw |first1=Kyle |title=A Victory for the Student Researcher: Chou v. University of Chicago |journal=Duke Law & Technology Review |volume=1 |issue=1 |date=2001 |pages=1–7 |url=https://scholarship.law.duke.edu/dltr/vol1/iss1/35/}}</ref><ref name="herrington_2010">{{cite book |last1=Herrington |first1=TyAnna K. |title=Intellectual property on campus : students' rights and responsibilities |date=2010 |publisher=Southern Illinois University Press |isbn=9780809385843}}</ref>{{rp|25–6}}.

== Personal life and death ==
Roizman's wife Betty was a [[Law library|legal librarian]]; they married in 1950. He had a son, Arthur. Roizman died in Chicago on April 13, 2026, at the age of 96.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-04-20 |title=Bernard Roizman, ScD, pioneering virologist, 1929–2026 {{!}} Biological Sciences Division {{!}} The University of Chicago |url=https://biologicalsciences.uchicago.edu/news/bernard-roizman-obituary |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=biologicalsciences.uchicago.edu |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Longman |first=Jeré |date=June 4, 2026 |title=Bernard Roizman, Virologist Who Demystified Herpes, Dies at 96 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/04/science/bernard-roizman-dead.html |access-date=June 5, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref>
